stemMd:
> Under the faculty's regulations, a student may sit the oral examination in Roman Law only after passing the written test. A student who passes the written test with distinction does not sit the oral examination: the written mark becomes the final mark. Luca sat the oral examination in Roman Law in July.

Which of the following can be deduced from the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Luca passed the written test, but not with distinction.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Luca passed the written test with distinction.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Luca passed the oral examination in Roman Law.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Luca passed the written test at his first attempt.

explanationMd:
Use each rule on the one fact given about Luca: he sat the oral examination.

**First rule.** The oral may be sat *only after* passing the written test. Luca sat the oral, so he had passed the written test.

**Second rule.** A student who passes the written test with distinction does *not* sit the oral. Luca did sit it, so he did not pass with distinction.

Together: Luca passed the written test, but not with distinction. Both halves are forced by the text.

**How to check.** Sort the other statements. That he passed with distinction is **false** — it would have kept him out of the oral. Whether he passed the oral, and whether he passed the written test at his first attempt, are **not deducible**: the text says nothing about the result of the oral or about how many attempts he made.

distractorRationale.c: Not deducible. The text says Luca sat the oral examination, not how he did in it. Sitting an examination and passing it are different things.
distractorRationale.b: False on the text. Students who pass with distinction do not sit the oral examination, and Luca did sit it, so he cannot have passed with distinction.
distractorRationale.d: Not deducible. The text establishes that Luca passed the written test at some point before July, but says nothing about how many attempts it took him.

accessibilityText: A true, false or not deducible question. The text says that, under the faculty's regulations, a student may sit the oral examination in Roman Law only after passing the written test; a student who passes the written test with distinction does not sit the oral, because the written mark becomes the final mark; and Luca sat the oral examination in Roman Law in July. The question asks which statement can be deduced. The four answer options are: Luca passed the written test, but not with distinction; Luca passed the written test with distinction; Luca passed the oral examination in Roman Law; Luca passed the written test at his first attempt.

provenance.notes: Original true / false / not-deducible item: two rules applied to one fact yield a deducible statement, while the distractors are one false statement and two not-deducible ones. Faculty and student are invented.

review.author: bocconi-law-wave8-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Sitting the oral requires having passed the written test, and passing with distinction removes the oral. Since Luca sat the oral, he passed the written test without distinction. 'Passed with distinction' is therefore false, while passing the oral and passing the written test at the first attempt are not deducible. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-final-verbal-run1) reached the same answer: Sitting the oral requires passing the written test, and a pass with distinction means no oral, so Luca passed without distinction. 'With distinction' contradicts the text. Passing the oral and passing at the first attempt are not stated.]
